newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SHAREHOLDER BZ CALLS CS OFFER FOR WINTERTHUR FAIR.
newsitem.headline: SHAREHOLDER BZ CALLS CS OFFER FOR WINTERTHUR FAIR.

text.p: Terms of a proposed merger between Swiss financial group Credit Suisse and insurer Winterthur Group, announced Monday, were seen as fair by major shareholder, Swiss investment group BZ.

"Our official statement is that it we see it as a reasonable industrial solution, which would be done at a fair price," said Stefan Holzer, a spokesman and vice director for BZ Trust, part of the investment group run by investor Martin Ebner.
The group and its customers currently hold roughly 30 percent of Winterthur, Holzer said.
Elaborating on Holzer's comments, BZ Group board member Kurt Schildknecht said roughly 25 percent of the stake was held by the group, and roughly a further five percent by customers of BZ Bank.
Schildknecht said the merger between the financial giant and Switzerland's third-largest insurer made sense.
"It it concerns productivity... product development... and distribution," he said.
The separate boards of directors at BK Group's investment funds BK Vision and Stillhalter Vision must still approve terms for the merger, the officials said.
Schildknecht declined to say whether the Group regarded its current stake in Winterthur as a long-term investment or not.
"We think it is a good solution at a fair price," he said.
Before the merger was announced, BZ Trust, in a shareholder letter, spelled out different scenarios for Winterthur.
BZ Trust recalled in the letter that it has said it was seeking a stake of over 50 percent in the insurer.
However, the letter, dated August 6, also dwelled on prospects for cooperation between Winterthur and a large international insurer.
Another possibility would be that CS would make an offer for Winterthur. It said the outcome of such a merger with CS would be positive for both the insurer and the banking group.
The letter noted that in case CS did make such an offer, this would give Ebner's shareholders a large unspecified stake in CS.
"The old shareholders in Winterthur -- and with them, especially BK Vision and Stillhalter Vision -- would become a significant shareholder group in the Credit Suisse Group," BZ Trust said.
